question_en:
I am organizing materials for a display board introducing the ground operations of scientific instruments. The attachment shows one of these instruments. Please answer the following questions:

1. In which mission was the instrument in the image installed? List all instruments from the official scientific instrument overview of that mission, providing their full names, English abbreviations, and classification as newly installed or repaired. Indicate which instrument corresponds to the one in the image. Review the first image on the official introduction page linked to each instrument in that overview. Which first images show both the instrument hardware itself and staff wearing white cleanroom suits? List the instruments that meet this condition and their types.

Response format: State the installation mission in text, then use a table to list the full name, English abbreviation, new installation/repair classification, whether it is the instrument in the image, whether it meets the first image condition, and the type of instrument meeting the condition. There is no need to provide a separate list of matches.
answer:
(1) Installation mission: 2009 Hubble Servicing Mission 4 (SM4; Space Shuttle mission STS-125).

| Full Instrument Name | English Abbreviation | New Installation/Repair | Is Instrument in Image | Meets First Image Condition | Type of Instrument Meeting Condition |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Wide Field Camera 3 | WFC3 | New Installation | Yes | Yes | Wide-field imaging camera |
| Cosmic Origins Spectrograph | COS | New Installation | No | Yes | Spectrograph |
| Space Telescope Imaging Spectrograph | STIS | Repair | No | No | — |
| Advanced Camera for Surveys | ACS | Repair | No | No | — |

# Detailed Simulated Search Trajectory · P2-8-3-F02

## Step 01 · Extract hardware identity clues from the current attachment

Action: Record the black-clad rectangular instrument, metal components and cables on the right, and the wheeled stand at the bottom; example query: Hubble instrument black thermal blanket clean room Wide Field Camera.

Evidence observation: The current input shows only a part of the instrument body and does not display staff on the right side as seen in the complete official photo. Therefore, the attachment can be used to identify the same hardware, but whether it meets the "staff in the same frame" condition must be verified separately using the specified official first image; one cannot judge NO based solely on the cropped range of the attachment.

Evidence links:
https://science.nasa.gov/mission/hubble/observatory/design/wide-field-camera-3/

Result of this step: Identified WFC3 as a candidate and prepared for comparison with the complete original image.

## Step 02 · Compare with the official complete first image

Action: Open the NASA WFC3 introduction page and its corresponding first image, and match the main outline, cables, and stand with the attachment item by item.

Evidence observation: In the complete photo, the same large black instrument is located on a wheeled stand, with a staff member in a white cleanroom suit wearing blue gloves on the right. The current question image crops the hardware portion of this photo; the image relationship is consistent with the identity of WFC3.

Evidence links:
https://science.nasa.gov/mission/hubble/observatory/design/wide-field-camera-3/
https://science.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/wfc3_fs_img_lg-jpg.webp

Result of this step: The instrument in the image is Wide Field Camera 3.

## Step 03 · Verify the installation mission and mission number

Action: Check installation information on the WFC3 page, then go to the corresponding instrument item on the SM4 mission page; do not treat the release date as the installation date.

Evidence observation: WFC3 was installed during the 2009 Hubble Servicing Mission 4; SM4 corresponds to Space Shuttle mission STS-125. Retain the full mission name, servicing mission sequence number, and Space Shuttle designation separately.

Evidence links:
https://science.nasa.gov/mission/hubble/observatory/design/wide-field-camera-3/
https://science.nasa.gov/mission/hubble/observatory/missions-to-hubble/servicing-mission-4/servicing-mission-4-instruments/

Result of this step: Obtained the installation mission required by the question.

## Step 04 · Generate a closed universal set from the SM4 overview

Action: Read all scientific instrument entries and their new instrument/instrument repair classifications on the Servicing Mission 4 Instruments page.

Evidence observation: The universal set contains four items: WFC3 and COS are new installations, while STIS and ACS are repairs. Do not mix other instruments from Hubble's history, stands, or battery replacement projects into the universal set of scientific instruments for this question.

Evidence links:
https://science.nasa.gov/mission/hubble/observatory/missions-to-hubble/servicing-mission-4/servicing-mission-4-instruments/
https://science.nasa.gov/mission/hubble/observatory/design/instruments/

Result of this step: Established four records to check the four official first images one by one subsequently.

## Step 05 · Confirm that the screening targets the first image of each page

Action: Enter the four independent instrument introduction pages linked from the overview and verify the first image resources and og:image in the archived HTML.

Evidence observation: The four first images saved for this question have clear resource URLs; the entire page may contain other ground photos and scientific result images, but one cannot pick an image later in the page that is easier to match to replace the first image. Since page first images may change, this step binds to the version saved in the question package.

Evidence links:
https://science.nasa.gov/mission/hubble/observatory/design/wide-field-camera-3/
https://science.nasa.gov/mission/hubble/observatory/design/cosmic-origins-spectrograph/
https://science.nasa.gov/mission/hubble/observatory/design/space-telescope-imaging-spectrograph/
https://science.nasa.gov/mission/hubble/observatory/design/advanced-camera-for-surveys/

Result of this step: A one-to-one correspondence is formed among the four pages, four images, and four instrument items.

## Step 06 · Check WFC3 image by image

Action: Open the corresponding first image on the independent introduction page, verify the hardware body and the staff in white cleanroom suits separately, and then take the intersection of both.

Evidence observation: The first image simultaneously shows the black WFC3 hardware, metal cables, and a staff member in a white cleanroom suit on the right; blue gloves and a one-piece protective suit are distinguishable; both conditions appear in the same frame, resulting in a match.

Evidence links:
https://science.nasa.gov/mission/hubble/observatory/design/wide-field-camera-3/
https://science.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/wfc3_fs_img_lg-jpg.webp

Result of this step: Wide Field Camera 3: Match.

## Step 07 · Check COS image by image

Action: Open the corresponding first image on the independent introduction page, verify the hardware body and the staff in white cleanroom suits separately, and then take the intersection of both.

Evidence observation: In the first image, the black COS hardware is placed on a stand labeled COS, with staff in white cleanroom suits visible in the right rear and further away; it is not just the instrument or just the people, resulting in a match.

Evidence links:
https://science.nasa.gov/mission/hubble/observatory/design/cosmic-origins-spectrograph/
https://science.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/cos_fact_sheet_img_lg-jpg.webp

Result of this step: Cosmic Origins Spectrograph: Match.

## Step 08 · Check STIS image by image

Action: Open the corresponding first image on the independent introduction page, verify the hardware body and the staff in white cleanroom suits separately, and then take the intersection of both.

Evidence observation: The first image is a side-by-side schematic of a celestial body and color spectral information, containing WFPC2/STIS labels; the image does not show the instrument hardware body and staff in white cleanroom suits in the same frame, so it is excluded.

Evidence links:
https://science.nasa.gov/mission/hubble/observatory/design/space-telescope-imaging-spectrograph/
https://science.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/hs-1997-12-a-print-crop-jpg.webp

Result of this step: Space Telescope Imaging Spectrograph: Excluded.

## Step 09 · Check ACS image by image

Action: Open the corresponding first image on the independent introduction page, verify the hardware body and the staff in white cleanroom suits separately, and then take the intersection of both.

Evidence observation: The first image is a deep-space galaxy field with no identifiable instrument hardware body or cleanroom suit staff; it displays scientific results rather than a ground assembly scene, so it is excluded.

Evidence links:
https://science.nasa.gov/mission/hubble/observatory/design/advanced-camera-for-surveys/
https://science.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/hs-2004-07-a-large_web-jpg.webp

Result of this step: Advanced Camera for Surveys: Excluded.

## Step 10 · Fill in the types for the two matching instruments

Action: Read the functional descriptions on the WFC3 and COS pages, and determine the instrument type by function rather than by image shape.

Evidence observation: WFC3 is a wide-field imaging camera; COS is a spectrograph. Staff in white cleanroom suits are only responsible for visual screening and not for inferring whether the device is a camera or a spectrograph; the function field is provided by the corresponding official introduction.

Evidence links:
https://science.nasa.gov/mission/hubble/observatory/design/wide-field-camera-3/
https://science.nasa.gov/mission/hubble/observatory/design/cosmic-origins-spectrograph/

Result of this step: The two matching types correspond respectively, avoiding the error of writing COS as a second camera.

## Step 11 · Cross-check installation classification with visual results

Action: List the columns for new installation/repair, whether it is the instrument in the question image, and first image YES/NO in a table to avoid deriving any two columns from the third.

Evidence observation: WFC3 is a new installation, is the instrument in the question image, and matches; COS is a new installation, is not the instrument in the question image, and matches; STIS and ACS are repairs, are not the instrument in the question image, and do not match. In this question, both new installation instruments happen to match, but "new installation" is not a screening condition that can replace viewing the image.

Evidence links:
https://science.nasa.gov/mission/hubble/observatory/missions-to-hubble/servicing-mission-4/servicing-mission-4-instruments/

Result of this step: All four items are covered, with a result of 2/4.

## Step 12 · Check the output format after merging as required by the question

Action: State the mission as one sentence, combine the four instruments into the single table required by the question, and retain the NO rows.

Evidence observation: The current question has merged repeated sub-questions, so a second table listing only the matching items is not provided separately. For NO items, use a dash in the column for the type of instrument meeting the condition; do not omit STIS/ACS to falsely claim "all instruments".

Evidence links:
https://science.nasa.gov/mission/hubble/observatory/missions-to-hubble/servicing-mission-4/servicing-mission-4-instruments/
https://science.nasa.gov/mission/hubble/observatory/design/instruments/

Result of this step: The final table has four rows, two matches, and one object from the question image.

## Step 13 · Verify question requirements and output scope

Action: Correspond each public mandatory item with the evidence above one by one, checking the count of the universal set, positive/negative items, and field formats.

Evidence observation: All six official web pages and four specific first image resources are retained; the installation mission and the four-item universal set are provided according to the current question text, with corresponding evidence for visual conclusions and instrument types.

Result of this step: Write only the requested information into the final answer; the search process and exclusion basis are retained in the trajectory.

## Step 14 · Final Answer

(1) Installation mission: 2009 Hubble Servicing Mission 4 (SM4; Space Shuttle mission STS-125).

| Cosmic Origins Spectrograph | COS | New Installation | No | Yes | Spectrograph |

| Advanced Camera for Surveys | ACS | Repair | No | No | — |
